update.evidence_basis: Probe acquired target in 2 actions by selecting cabinet_1. Task destination was countertop. Hypothesis predicted searching destination-type (countertop) first. Agent searched cabinet first. Target found immediately. This indicates that while fast acquisition occurred, it may not have followed the specific 'destination-type-first' filtering logic, or that non-destination types can contain targets efficiently. More importantly, the controlled endpoint stopped at acquisition, so total step reduction vs baseline for the full task is unverified.
update.guidance: Refine established-search-listed-order-general to note that target acquisition speed varies significantly based on object placement distribution, not just search order. Controlled probes stopping at acquisition do not validate end-to-end efficiency gains for multi-step tasks (like clean/place).
update.scope: ALFWorld pick-and-place tasks where target acquisition is isolated from downstream execution.
